A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DRK research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary sections are readable and support comparison, including content moved between sections.

before.justification: V1 reports original rendering experiments on DiverseScenes, Mip-NeRF360, NeRF-Synthetic, and Tank&Temple, plus ablations, camera-noise tests, and mesh-conversion demonstrations.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in the main paper and supplementary material, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and robustness tests.

M1.justification: The reported basis-angle activation offset changes from 1/(K−1) in v1 Section 4.5 to 1/(K−2) in v2 Section S4. This revises the documented parameter mapping; the remaining kernel components, rasterization procedures, and mesh conversion are retained. Implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same ten DiverseScenes scenes, Mip-NeRF360, NeRF-Synthetic, and nine Tank&Temple scenes. Mesh conversion and noisy-camera scenarios already appear in v1's supplement.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain 2D-GS, 3D-GS, 3D-HGS, and GES. The additional 3D-GS(L) configuration remains in Table 3 despite losing its explanatory sentence. Newly cited 3D Convex Splatting is not added as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Dataset splits, metrics, foreground masking, 35K training steps, learning rates, sparsity thresholds, and camera-noise levels remain unchanged. The new sentence reversing S1/S2 density order contradicts retained settings and counts; it does not establish a changed experimental configuration.

E4.justification: The sharpening, curvature, and basis-count ablations move from v1 Section 5.4/Table 4 to v2 Section S3/Table S4 without changed evidence. Camera-noise tests, sorting analysis, and mesh-conversion demonstrations are also retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Camera-noise standard deviations describe input perturbations, and their reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All matched numerical tables and benchmark findings are retained. V2 Section 5.1 adds an incorrect textual density ranking, DRK → S2 → S1. Table 2 in both versions instead gives 260K primitives for DRK, 109K for S1, and 42K for S2. This is a reporting change, not improved measured performance.

T1.justification: Alongside the activation-offset revision, the stated angular bound changes from π/2 to π in the parameterization discussion. This changes the mathematical specification. Equations 1–13 and the Gaussian-special-case derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about flexible primitives, rendering quality, efficiency, and DiverseScenes. The expanded conclusion highlights training-free mesh conversion, which v1 already claimed and demonstrated in Section S1.

C2.justification: V2 elaborates prospective deferred rendering through albedo, roughness, and metallicity maps and names editing, VR, and AR applications. The standalone limitations summary disappears, although weak-supervision and camera-noise limitations remain discussed in Sections 5.2 and S3.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's explanation that 3D-GS(L) uses an adjusted densification threshold while retaining its results. The angular activation detail is revised. Other parameterization and training details move from Section 4.5 to Section S4 without substantive changes.

R1.justification: V2 adds Held et al.'s 3D Convex Splatting and acknowledges it as concurrent work in the introduction and related work. The other cited works are retained; the broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized reorganization moves optimization and ablations into the supplement and promotes mesh conversion into Section 5.4. V2 expands the conclusion, adds acknowledgements and a density explanation, and removes the standalone limitations paragraph. Most prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 uses sharper image assets, and the mesh-conversion schematic is visually revised and moved from Figure S1 to Figure 10. The ablation table moves into the supplement, supplementary tables are reordered, and surrounding layout changes. Existing benchmark panels and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The angular-offset and bound correction improves the mathematical consistency of the method specification, and acknowledging concurrent 3D Convex Splatting improves positioning. These support a limited overall gain. V2 also introduces a density-order error and removes the 3D-GS(L) configuration explanation, reducing experimental clarity. The empirical evidence remains unchanged.
